clue.text: Uncast replacements?

parts.note: read as roles in a play that no actor has been given, these are surplus pieces kept for swapping in when something breaks

explanation.definitionFit: Spares are replacement components, and the theatrical reading adds roles left uncast.

clue.text: The dog's first — it comes romping home

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word dog's
romping suggests the letters frolicking about into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A dog is first to bound back into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives D from dog's, and 'romping' turns IT COMES into OMESTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Home affairs are domestic affairs: the adjective means relating to one's own country or household.

clue.text: Fighting a case

definitions.meaning: combat, as soldiers see in battle
a lawsuit brought before a court

explanation.definitionFit: Troops see combat as this, and a lawsuit is also called by this word.

clue.text: Part of a building — birds may be on it

definitions.meaning: an extension projecting from the main block
birds in flight are said to be on this

explanation.definitionFit: A building's annexe is so named, and flying birds are said to be on this.

clue.text: Camaraderie sought by ambitious academics

definitions.meaning: a paid research post or membership of a college or learned society

explanation.definitionFit: Companionship is one sense; a college research post that scholars compete for is the other.

clue.text: Indisposed star can't perform

indicators.note: indisposed means out of order, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A leading actor falls ill and cannot go on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct or carry out business is to perform it; a synonym.

clue.text: Make fresh point about university and exit temporarily

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece
making something fresh means remaking it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A student revises an argument about university and then pops out for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make fresh' turns POINT into NIPOT, and 'about' wraps that around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Popping out briefly, to return soon, is an informal phrasal verb for a short exit.

clue.text: Go to get added flavour

definitions.meaning: energy and enthusiasm, as in 'full of go'
grated citrus peel used to flavour food

explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiasm and vigour is one sense; grated lemon or orange peel used in cooking is the other.

clue.text: Ban student's aid in passage for translation

indicators.note: in places the aid inside the passage

parts.note: a prose is a passage set for translation into a foreign language in school exercises
a crib is a translation or set of answers a student uses illicitly

explanation.surface: Schools forbid using a crib on a translation exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit or outlaw something is a direct synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Rebel without a cause

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for rebel goes round the letter

parts.note: to rise up is to rebel

explanation.surface: The film title about a troubled youth who defies authority for no clear reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebel Without a Cause' is a 1955 James Dean film; 'without' means outside, putting A inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a laugh or a doubt is to cause it; a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Adjusting, freeing, or gathering sails

indicators.note: adjusting means altering the arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Sailors trim, loosen or furl the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: To reef is to take in part of a sail to reduce its area, so this is gathering sails.

clue.text: Rank play by forwards

parts.note: in rugby the forwards stand in two parallel ranks to contest a ball thrown in from touch

explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union, not familiar everywhere: the restart after the ball goes into touch, contested by the forwards standing in two lines.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union this restart has the forwards line up in rows for a throw-in.

clue.text: Point out a device for climbers

indicators.note: out signals the letters being knocked out of their order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone explains a piece of mountaineering gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal spike hammered into rock to hold a rope is this climbing aid.

clue.text: Modern home for an Englishman in the northeast

parts.note: modern means new
from the saying that an Englishman's home is his castle

explanation.surface: A new house for an Englishman living up in the northeast of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An Englishman's home is his castle' is a British proverb; Newcastle upon Tyne is the chief city of northeast England.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is loose: the answer is a city located in northeast England.

clue.text: Its residents think life is barely worth living

definitions.text: Its residents think life is barely worth living

parts.words: Its residents think life is barely worth living
parts.note: barely is read as unclothed: people who live naked think that is the only life worth having

explanation.definitionFit: A holiday site for naturists, whose residents live barely in the sense of unclothed.

clue.text: Put in a difficult position and finished full of rage

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the word for finished holds the word for rage

parts.note: finished means ended
rage means anger

explanation.surface: Someone was threatened, and the encounter ended in fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil something is to place it at risk, a close synonym.

clue.text: Is he the highest-ever bidder for bloodstock?

definitions.text: Is he the highest-ever bidder for bloodstock?

parts.words: Is he the highest-ever bidder for bloodstock?
parts.note: Shakespeare's king cries 'My kingdom for a horse!', offering a whole realm for one thoroughbred

explanation.walkthrough: Bloodstock means thoroughbred horses; the bid is the line 'A horse! a horse! my kingdom for a horse!'
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's English king offers his kingdom for a horse at Bosworth, an unbeatable bid for a racehorse.

clue.text: Put some notes in order?

parts.note: musical notes set out for instruments or voices, not just papers tidied

explanation.definitionFit: Music adapted for particular instruments is said to have been set in order this way.

clue.text: Romantic details I made up

indicators.note: made up means invented or put together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A dreamer admits inventing the specifics.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic, as a noun, is a dreamer guided by ideals rather than practicality.

clue.text: Settles, or prepares to fight

definitions.meaning: pays what is owed, settling a debt
takes up a boxing stance facing an opponent

explanation.definitionFit: Paying off a debt is one sense; adopting a fighting stance is the other.

clue.text: Strongly advise one not to lose heart — it's most important

parts.note: to urge someone is to advise them strongly

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word not is dropped

explanation.surface: Encouragement not to despair matters above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose heart' drops the O from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressing that demands attention first is treated as of highest priority.

clue.text: Don't get up early — about one is right

indicators.note: about means round, so the word for right goes round the numeral

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice to sleep late: around one o'clock is the proper time to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside LIEN; 'is' is a link. The surface makes 'about one' sound like a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay in bed late in the morning is the phrasal verb meant.

clue.text: See fresh hate put upon hate

indicators.note: put upon means placed on top, which in a down entry puts the first piece above

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Fresh loathing is piled on old loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges HATE into ATHE, and 'put upon' places LO above it.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest or abhor intensely is this verb, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fundamental shifting in cargo

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A basic problem with freight moving in the hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something structural and inherent to the whole is basic in this sense.

clue.text: Resistance units in the employment of the Queen

definitions.meaning: the SI units of electrical resistance

definitions.text: in the employment of the Queen
definitions.meaning: the initials On Her Majesty's Service, stamped on official mail

explanation.definitionFit: Electrical resistance is measured in these units; the same letters abbreviate On Her Majesty's Service.

clue.text: It's read with feeling

parts.note: with feeling means by touch, not with emotion: raised dots read by fingertips

explanation.definitionFit: The raised-dot writing system for blind readers is read by touch.

clue.text: Old monk reciting part of the rosary

indicators.note: reciting means saying out loud, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a rosary is a string of beads used to count prayers

explanation.surface: An elderly monk telling his rosary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was an eighth-century Northumbrian monk and scholar.

clue.text: Game Italian composer — not Verdi

indicators.note: not signals that the named composer's letters are left out

parts.note: Monteverdi was an Italian composer of early opera
taken as written

explanation.surface: A game Italian composer, but not Verdi.
explanation.walkthrough: MONTEVERDI minus VERDI. Three-card monte is a card-trick betting game.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game for gambling, as in three-card monte, is called by this name.

clue.text: Didn't dally as the Dame in variety

indicators.note: in variety means in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A performer hurried along playing the pantomime Dame in a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in variety' rearranges AS THE DAME. The Dame is the British pantomime role played by a man in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry or move quickly is the opposite of dallying, so this phrase means did not linger.
